accuracy.evidence: Framed on the IB PYP PSPE learning outcomes cited by the topic (PSPE-ID-CU-P2-2, PSPE-ID-LO-P2-8): recognising that others have feelings and viewpoints and using that understanding in stories and interactions. The two 'where will she look' rounds are faithful versions of the Sally-Anne / unexpected-transfer false-belief task (Wimmer & Perner 1983; Baron-Cohen, Leslie & Frith 1985), and the adult text separates the cognitive part (theory of mind) from the affective part (empathy) as the research literature does. No claim is made that perspective-taking means agreeing.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets egocentric projection (assuming others feel what you would: the dog round where Kit+excited says 'You may love dogs, but Kit was knocked over'), the curse of knowledge in false belief (Mia/Raj rounds: 'We saw Tom move it, but Mia did not'), confusing the actor's and the victim's feeling (Ben+sorry, Zara+sad), judging a feeling as wrong (challenge 'wrongfeel'), and hostile attribution bias, jumping to 'on purpose' (Kai puddle round and 'purpose' feedback).

lab_distinct.evidence: Built on perspective-taking itself: comic strips that show an event the character missed and ask where they will look, feeling cards handed to characters whose pasts differ, reasons sorted to the child whose position produces them, and replies judged by whether they voice the other side. It passed the 30% shingle gate against every flagship, and none of the other emotion labs (flagfeel, flagmood, flagemo, flagcause, flaginfer) asks what another person knows or saw.

lab_teaches.evidence: The order builds the skill: one moment felt two ways (Ben and Zara), then 'what do they know' with two false-belief stories, then two fair sides in a quarrel, then the same event filtered through three different pasts, and finally using all of it to pick a reply. The learner commits a choice each time and the card text confirms why it fits; the step summary states the rule only after the learner has done it.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Do Ben and Zara feel the same? Yes' (they do not), 'Where will Mia look first? The red box, where it is now' (the classic false-belief error, disproved when only the blue box is accepted), and 'Will all three children feel the same about a friendly dog? Yes, the dog is friendly' (three different cards are needed).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with thirteen distinct m= messages that each name the slip: 'only sand to you', waves have no feelings, 'you know it is under the bed, Max was outside', nobody just knows, feelings are not right or wrong, two people can feel two ways, picture your first day, blaming skips her side, 'Oops!' is a clue, bumping back starts a fight, only your side, calling an idea silly.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores 0.3 against the family kid limit of 5.0 and adult text 5.7 against 10.0 (learn/readability.py). Canvas uses one-line stories and a one-line question in large type; card text is a name plus a three-to-five word clue such as 'A dog knocked her over'.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and the 12% duplicate gate. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (two views of one moment, shoes question, people only know what they saw, past events, kind words); adult paragraphs give the standard, the thinking/feeling split, named mistakes, and what the lab does. The family tip is two concrete reading questions.

mobile.evidence: Checked every step at 360 px light and iPhone 13 dark (shot.cjs): comic panels, three person cards and three feeling cards fit without clipping; long reply cards stack one per row on phones and wrap to two lines; drag targets are full-width cards about 130 px tall, and the button pad gives large tap targets below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: every task completes with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors. Every drag has a two-tap button route (Pick a card, then Give to a person or place, plus Pick again); the canvas aria-label and the hidden read-out restate the story, question and result after each move.
